newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: OSCE's Vranitzky to return to Tirana with report.
newsitem.headline: OSCE's Vranitzky to return to Tirana with report.

text.p: Former Austrian chancellor Franz Vranitzky, special envoy to Albania for Europe's top security body, will return to Tirana on Thursday to present his findings on the current crisis, officials said.

Vranitzky, who visited Albania on Saturday to assess the spreading chaos in the Balkan state, would also seek government approval for the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) to become involved in fresh general elections.
"Vranitzky will present his report to President Sali Berisha and new Prime Minister Bashkim Fino," an OSCE spokeswoman said on Wednesday.
Earlier, in Copenhagen, Vranitzky presented his findings to OSCE chairman-in-office, Danish Foreign Minister Niels Helveg Petersen.

In the report, faxed to Reuters in Vienna, he called on all sides in the conflict to show restraint and warned: "Violence by any side could spark a civil conflict of unforeseen dimension, plunging the country in a state of war."
Vranitzky said it was of "foremost importance" to continue an all-party dialogue in order to resolve a political and economic crisis engulfing the impoverished country.

He said a transitional government, to be formed by Berisha in consultation with his Democratic Party and the opposition, should resolve unrest in the south through political means, restore confidence in democracy and ensure the respect of fundamental human rights.

Vranitzky urged the OSCE to assist in talks between Tirana and southern cities in rebel hands, consider monitoring the collection of insurgents' weapons and help in the organisation of parliamentary elections, which must be held by June.
"In this effort special attention will need to be addressed to the electoral framework, full respect of the freedom of media, freedom of expression and freedom of association," the report said.
Vranitzky repeated international calls for a new constitution and urged international financial institutions to dispatch teams to assess Albania's economic situation.
